title: Module 2 Vocabulary Check
intro: Answer each item. Feedback comes right away. Items you miss come back for a retry round.

items.q: The mean of a set of scores is
o: The sum of the scores divided by the number of scores
The highest score minus the lowest
items.why: The mean is the balance point of the distribution, computed as the sum of scores divided by n.

o: The score that splits the ordered distribution into two equal halves
items.why: It is the 50th percentile. It depends on rank order, not on how extreme the extreme scores are.

o: The most frequently occurring score or category
items.why: The mode is the only measure of central tendency that works for nominal data.

o: A score divided by the mean
The square root of the variance
The difference between the highest and lowest scores
items.why: X minus the mean. Deviations from the mean always sum to zero.

items.q: The sum of squared deviations from the mean is abbreviated
items.why: SS stands for sum of squares. It is the starting point for variance and standard deviation.

items.q: Which measure of variability depends only on two scores?
items.why: The range uses only the highest and lowest scores, which makes it sensitive to outliers.

items.q: The standard deviation can be described as
o: The typical distance of scores from the mean
The average of the raw scores
items.why: It puts variability back into the original units of measurement.

items.q: A distribution with a long tail toward the high scores is
items.why: The direction of skew is the direction of the tail, not the direction of the bulk of the scores.

items.q: If a constant is added to every score, the standard deviation
items.why: Adding a constant shifts all scores, including the mean, and leaves the spread unchanged.

items.q: If every score is multiplied by 3, the standard deviation
items.why: Multiplying by a constant stretches the scale, and the standard deviation stretches with it. The variance is multiplied by 9.
